text:
maria: Heads-up — after the RBAC cleanup this morning a customer reported their historical DB backups fail to mount. Error from our restore job: `access denied: decrypt failed`.
josh: which backup? can you paste the job id / log snippet?
maria: job id restore-job-2026-03-23-079, stack:
```
2026-03-23T10:02:12Z ERROR restore: decrypt: AccessDeniedException
2026-03-23T10:02:12Z INFO backup_id=proj-42/db-snap-20260219
```
We saw an IAM change to uploader service account earlier: removed role storage.objectAdmin and tightened key access perms.
oliver: probably KMS grant missing from the uploader-sa on the CMEK. Did the RBAC change prune the kms:Decrypt grant? @tara any policy change PR?
tara: I approved the RBAC PR #8345 that removed a broad role binding, replaced with narrower ones. I didn't touch KMS key policy though. But cloud audit shows a deny on `projects/prod/keys/db-backup-key` around 09:58 UTC.
maria: audit log snippet:
`protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="uploader-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" protoPayload.status.code=7`
josh: code 7 = PERMISSION_DENIED. Two quick checks: 1) does the key have a condition rejecting requests from that SA? 2) did the key rotate to a new key version with different grants?
oliver: run `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy db-backup-key --location=global --keyring=redwood-backups` — check for a binding to uploader-sa or to the uploader service account's KMS cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter role.
maria: ran it — the key policy now only binds `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` to `serviceAccount:backup-processor@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and to a group `ops-kms@redwood.com`. uploader-sa is not listed.
tara: that explains it. RBAC cleanup removed broader storage-level perms but didn't update the KMS key policy to include the delegated uploader identity.
josh: mitigation options:
- temporarily grant uploader-sa the KMS role (fastest)
- roll back RBAC PR (broader) — noisy
- modify backup pipeline to use backup-processor SA for decrypt (requires config change + deploy)

Given customer impact, temporary grant sounds best. @oncall: can we do a temporary grant with a 1-hour TTL and create a tracking ticket?
maria: I've applied the grant to kms key with `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding db-backup-key --member=serviceAccount:uploader-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` and re-ran the restore: now works.
deploy-bot: CI job `restore-integration/2026-03-23` passed — https://ci.redwood.internal/restore-integration/2026-03-23
oliver: next steps (action items):
- (SEC) verify why uploader-sa needs direct KMS decrypt vs encrypt-only flow. If uploader should never decrypt, we need a wrapper service.
- (SRE) update backup pipeline to use backup-processor SA for decrypt or add an explicit delegation flow.
- (ENG) add an audit alert for KMS policy changes for `db-backup-key` (low noise but high signal).
- (PO) contact affected customers with short incident note.
tara: I'll open a follow-up PR to reintroduce a scoped key binding and propose using Cloud KMS CryptoKey versioned grants instead of broad role bindings.
maria: filing ticket: ENGSEC-1421 "uploader-sa KMS grant missing after RBAC prune" with remediation steps and rollback logs.
josh: also add a playbook step: after RBAC changes, run `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` for all keys in `redwood-backups` keyring and diff against baseline.
maria: noted. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
_extra_note: Document follows agents.md schema: messages in 'text' as a single continuous string. No title field included.
